build_order: 1. Sequencing: a 'Next to start' group in tracker_review_queue driven by a per-topic sequence, a written first-20 order in the Spanish appendix, and a 25-minute Spanish session shape. Changes for her: every Spanish session opens with one named thing to do, and coverage moves visibly about every three days instead of sitting at 1%.

2. Word-level spaced review: log every gallery/flashcard item (not only misses) with a topic ref and a timeout/wrong note, add a read-only tracker_review_words tool that computes due words on a Leitner schedule, and give the app a 'Review' set built from it. Changes for her: the words she keeps missing (juega al, criquet, tenis de mesa) come back at 1, 3, 7 and 14 days instead of at random, and her favourite game becomes the revision engine.

3. Listening and reading-aloud modes in the app via the browser speech APIs (hear-it on every card, a listen-and-pick gallery, a three-play dictation mode, reading aloud with recognition where the sandbox allows it), registered as new practice sources. Changes for her: first exposure to Listening (25% of the qualification, currently zero) and to the pronunciation and dictation tasks; the phonics topics P01-P06 finally get evidence.
strengths: The practice pipeline is well engineered and should not be touched while building on it: client_run_id idempotency (php/lib/store.php lines 1164-1235), the attempted = correct + retry + incorrect check (php/lib/mcp.php lines 1700-1708), pooled rather than mean accuracy (README 'Accuracy on the board is always pooled'), void-never-delete, and 'practice never moves a status'.

Per-item logging already exists in the schema (practice_item: prompt, topic_ref, outcome, attempts_taken, note; php/lib/store.php lines 1195-1210). A spaced word queue needs no table change, only a read path and fuller logging.
Practice sources are declared data (php/lib/practice.php lines 30-39: 'a new activity needs no schema change'), so listening, dictation and reading-aloud modes can be registered without a migration.

The scoreboard she likes is protected by a golden snapshot (tests/golden/spanish-scoreboard.html, README 'The Spanish board is pinned'), and the design stance of self-referenced progress with no streaks or withholding is coherent with the objective; the gold star and record line are the right kind of reward.

The gallery gets several things right for a learner with ADHD: short games, immediate feedback, keyboard controls (app-template.jsx lines 577-596), an 800 ms feedback pause, and a 20% mix of earlier sets (interleaving) in every game.

The 100-topic seed tags grammar as well as themes and carries tiers, so Foundation-only and Higher-only work can be filtered (G41-G65, S16, P07 are H; S11-S13 are F). That is the right shape for the marker's per-topic marks-lost analysis.

The marker skill's discipline is excellent and specific: bands not points, quote the descriptor, major vs minor errors, count time frames, never invent the 15 translation elements, never mark pronunciation from a transcript, store raw not scaled marks, and the range-vs-accuracy diagnosis in Step 7 ('the remedies are opposite') is genuinely useful teaching information.

The Spanish appendix chooses the right behavioural metric (translation elements attempted, time-frame range) instead of copying the maths blanks count, and its NEA warning ('25% of the qualification which a private or home-educated candidate cannot sit without a centre') is honest.
The 3 Sep seed correction (session 4) shows the record being kept honest: 23 false loose ends cleared with evidence rather than silently edited.

findings.title: BUILD 1 of 3: the tracker cannot say what to learn next in Spanish, so the 100-topic list is a record, not a plan
findings.where: php/lib/mcp.php lines 899-1000 (tracker_review_queue handler); gcse-progress-tracker/references/subjects/spanish.md lines 70-74 ('Checkpoint duties: None recorded yet'); language-learning-platform/SKILL.md lines 83-96 (step 2)
findings.problem: The queue builds three groups only: ageing (status secure/examready), loose ends (`$loose = array_values(array_filter($all, static fn($t) => $t['watch'] && $t['status'] !== 'gap'));`) and gaps (`$gaps = array_values(array_filter($all, static fn($t) => $t['status'] === 'gap'));`). Spanish has 98 topics at notstarted and none at gap, so the live output today is 'Ageing: Nothing overdue. Loose ends: None recorded. Priority gaps: None — no topic is marked as a gap.' The 'what should I do today' tool returns nothing for the subject with the least coverage. The topic table has no sequence or prerequisite field, and the appendix has no order either, yet language-learning-platform step 2 tells Claude to use the tracker to see 'what's coming up next in spec order'. The list itself mixes units of very different size (T01-T09 are whole themes of hundreds of words; G39 'Spelling changes not credited' and G40 'Derivational morphology (Reading)' are spec bullet points; S10-S16 are exam tasks), so a topic count is not a workload.
findings.why_it_matters: For a student with ADHD who works largely alone, the cost of deciding what to do is the cost that stops the session starting. The maths pipeline solves this (maths-tutor-session: 'Start every session with one call'); Spanish has no equivalent, which is consistent with four games and two 'developing' topics in three weeks. At 278 days out, 71 Foundation-pathway topics need starting at one every 3.9 days (2.9 days if teaching stops when the speaking window opens on 1 April 2027).
findings.proposal: Three parts. (a) Add a nullable integer `sequence` column on topic (default = seed order) and a fourth group to tracker_review_queue: '### Next to start' listing the first five notstarted topics whose tier includes the subject's intended tier, ordered by sequence then ref, each with its resources, placed after Priority gaps. Replace the empty-state line 'Priority gaps: None — no topic is marked as a gap.' with the Next-to-start list so the tool never returns nothing for a fresh subject. (b) Write the order into spanish.md under a new heading '## Sequence (first twenty)': T10 core high-frequency vocabulary, P01-P06 phonics (needed for reading aloud and dictation, and cheap), G01 gender/plurals, G03 articles, G07 agreement, G21 present regular, G22/G23 present stem-change and irregular (already touched), G26 gustar, G12 subject pronouns, G19 negation, G20 questions, T01 identity and relationships, T04 free time (already developing), G33 near future, G29 preterite, T02 healthy living, G31 imperfect, T03 education and work, G27 modals + infinitive, T11 multi-word phrases; defer every H-only ref (G41-G65, S16, P07) until the tier decision. Mark this order as expert judgement to be checked against the sequencing evidence. (c) Add a short-session shape for Spanish, either as a new spanish-session skill or a section in language-learning-platform: 25 minutes = 5 min review set in the gallery, 10 min one sequenced unit taught with 6-10 new items added as an app set, 5 min production (flashcards self-rated or chat), 5 min log via tracker_log_practice and tracker_log_session. What it changes for her: every session opens with one named next thing, and a topic can move every few days, so the 1% badge starts moving.
findings.evidence_needed: Curriculum sequencing in MFL (high-frequency vocabulary and phonics first, e.g. Ofsted MFL research review 2021, NCELP schemes); reduction of task-initiation load for ADHD learners (decision cost, structured routines)

findings.title: BUILD 2 of 3: the missed-word data is already flowing but cannot drive a spaced review queue yet
findings.where: php/lib/mcp.php lines 641-720 (tracker_log_practice items schema) and 1760-1790 (item validation); php/lib/store.php lines 1195-1210 (items stored) and 1293-1299 (practiceItems, read only by getPracticeRun, which is called only by tracker_void_practice at mcp.php line 1999); README 'Per-item detail... the Spanish app supplies items only for the words missed'; live session 5 (2026-09-04) 'kept missing: juega al, criquet, juegas al, tenis de mesa, fútbol, juego al tenis de mesa juega tenis'
findings.problem: Five things are missing. (1) Only misses are logged, so a word that was missed on 18 Aug and got right on 4 Sep looks identical to one still being missed: recovery is invisible. (2) No item carries a topic_ref: tracker_practice_stats returns no per-topic table and the seeded 'Practice by topic' panel renders 'No practice carries a topic reference yet'. (3) There is no MCP read path for items at all; tracker_list_practice returns run counts only, so Claude cannot ask 'which words has she missed twice'. (4) Prompts are free text with no stable key, and one logged prompt ('juego al tenis de mesa juega tenis') is a garbled concatenation, so even a query by prompt would miscount. (5) No schedule: nothing records when a word is next due. The 'kept missing' list therefore lives only as prose in a session summary and the planned next step 'Re-drill the words she kept missing' depends on someone remembering it.
findings.why_it_matters: Spaced retrieval is the best-evidenced technique for vocabulary and she already does the retrieval part voluntarily. Right now the gallery samples uniformly with replacement (app-template.jsx line 469 `gameVocabulary[Math.floor(Math.random() * gameVocabulary.length)]`), so a word she has missed three times is no more likely to appear than one she has never missed. Her misses cluster on juego/juegas/juega, which is the person-ending point (G21/G22), not vocabulary, and the tracker cannot see that because no item has a grammar ref.
findings.proposal: (a) App and logging: log every item, not only misses, with `prompt` = the exact Spanish string as it appears in the set, `outcome` correct/incorrect, `note` = 'timeout' | 'wrong' | 'flash-not-yet', `topic_ref` = the set's theme ref (T04 for Sports) and a second item for the grammar ref where the set is grammar-led; keep runs under 200 items by logging one run per game. (b) Service: add a read-only tool `tracker_review_words(subject, limit=20, source?)` that groups non-void items by prompt and returns per word: times seen, times missed, last seen, last missed, box = consecutive corrects since the last miss, due = last_seen + [1,3,7,14,30][min(box,4)] days, sorted due-first; plus a `words` block on the practice board. (c) App: a 'Review' pseudo-set assembled from the due list; because the artifact sandbox can only reach api.anthropic.com, Claude pastes the JSON block at session start, or, better, host the app on the tracker domain so it can fetch the due list and POST runs directly (removing the model from the logging loop, which is also what causes the session-vs-run mismatch in the finding below). What it changes for her: the words she keeps missing come back at 1, 3, 7 and 14 days, the 'Review' set is short and winnable, and the Practice-by-topic panel starts showing which theme and which grammar point the misses belong to.
findings.evidence_needed: Spacing and retrieval-practice effects for L2 vocabulary (meta-analyses; expanding vs uniform intervals); whether spaced retrieval effects hold for learners with ADHD (likely general-population only, say so)

findings.title: BUILD 3 of 3: the app covers isolated word recognition only; listening, speaking, reading and writing have nothing
findings.where: language-learning-platform/assets/app-template.jsx: Flashcards lines 271-420 (no audio), Shooting Gallery lines 422-905 (Spanish shown, English picked from three), AI Chat lines 907-1249 (typed production only); gcse-spanish-marker/references/aqa-8692-assessment.md sections 2-5; php/lib/practice.php lines 30-39 (source registry)
findings.problem: Paper 1 Listening is 25% of the qualification and includes dictation (8 marks F / 10 H, 'sentences heard three times'); Paper 2 Speaking includes reading aloud with a 5-mark pronunciation grid and a photo card; Paper 3 Reading needs continuous text and inference of unknown words; Paper 4 Writing is band-marked on time frames and range. The app has no audio in any mode (flashcards show a phonetic guide only), no listening input, no speaking output, no continuous text and no timed writing task. All 16 S-strand topics and all 7 P-strand topics are notstarted and nothing in the pipeline can produce evidence for them. The chat's prompt types (lines 921-927: friend_casual, teacher_question, conversation_starter, practice_prompt, scenario) do not correspond to any AQA task.
findings.why_it_matters: Three of the four components cannot be practised with the tools she has, so the parts of the exam that reward output and listening will be met for the first time in a mock. Listening is also the component where Foundation is scaled x1.25 (spanish.md lines 22-28), so it carries more per raw mark. Audio also makes the vocabulary work itself stick better than text alone.
findings.proposal: Add three modes to the template, each a new registered source. (1) 'Hear it': a speaker button on every flashcard and gallery word using window.speechSynthesis with an es-ES voice; zero network. (2) 'Listen' gallery variant: the word is spoken, not shown; she picks the English (source spanish_listen). (3) Dictation: a set-level sentence is spoken three times, she types it, the app compares word by word and logs per-word items with note 'accent' | 'spelling' | 'missing' (source spanish_dictation; mirrors Paper 1 Section B). (4) Reading aloud with SpeechRecognition (lang es-ES) where the browser allows the microphone, scored by word match, logged to spanish_readaloud with topic_ref S04 and the P refs; if the artifact iframe blocks the microphone or speech APIs (unverified), host the page on the tracker domain instead. Register the sources by appending to PRACTICE_SOURCE_SEED: ['key' => 'spanish_listen', 'display_name' => 'Listen and pick', 'subject_slug' => 'spanish', 'metrics_schema' => []], ['key' => 'spanish_dictation', 'display_name' => 'Dictation', 'subject_slug' => 'spanish', 'metrics_schema' => ['words' => 'number']], ['key' => 'spanish_readaloud', 'display_name' => 'Reading aloud', 'subject_slug' => 'spanish', 'metrics_schema' => ['word_match' => 'number']]. For writing, a later '90-word builder' with three time-frame checkboxes (present, past, future) whose count is logged as metrics.time_frames, which is the appendix's own behavioural metric. What it changes for her: the first listening exposure of the course, pronunciation practice she can do alone, and evidence for S01, S02, S04 and P01-P06.
findings.evidence_needed: Dual-coding / audio-plus-text for vocabulary retention; benefit of early phonics and decoding in MFL (Ofsted MFL review 2021); feasibility of Web Speech API inside the artifact sandbox (technical check, not research)

findings.title: Decide the exam series and the speaking centre now; decide the tier at a dated checkpoint; the appendix and the subject row currently disagree
findings.where: gcse-progress-tracker/references/subjects/spanish.md lines 10-12 ('Tier intention | TO CONFIRM', 'Exam series | TO CONFIRM', 'Target grade | TO CONFIRM'), lines 49-59 (speaking NEA), lines 70-74 ('Checkpoint duties: None recorded yet'); live tracker_get_state header 'GCSE Spanish (AQA 8692, Higher)'
findings.problem: The subject row already says Higher while the appendix says the tier is undecided, so the dashboard and every get_state call present a decision that has not been made. Nothing names a centre, a centre deadline, a series go/no-go date or a tier decision date, and there are no checkpoint duties, so the progress-tracker skill's mandatory checkpoint step ('honour whatever it says') has nothing to honour. The speaking NEA is conducted in a five-week window in April-May and marked externally; a centre willing to host an external candidate's speaking test is a harder find than one hosting written papers, and the entries deadline for the June 2027 series is the same ~21 Feb 2027 that the maths appendix records.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a hard external dependency with a long lead time and it decides whether 25% of the grade exists at all. Tier can wait for evidence; centre and series cannot. It also frames the workload honestly: on a Foundation pathway 71 topics remain (one every 3.9 days to the exam), on Higher 95 (one every 2.9 days), alongside maths in May 2027. Whether June 2027 is the right series for Spanish is a real question given 1% coverage and that she would still be a year early in June 2028; it should be a dated decision, not a default.
findings.proposal: Fill the appendix rows now, replacing the three TO CONFIRM lines with: 'Tier intention | Foundation-safe pathway (all F/H topics first; H-only refs G41-G65, S16, P07 deferred). Higher held open until the tier decision on 2027-01-31.' 'Exam series | June 2027, go/no-go decision 2027-01-31 (entries close ~2027-02-21). If fewer than 30 F-pathway topics are secure by then, defer to June 2028.' 'Target grade | Working target 4, stretch 5 (Foundation ceiling). Revisit at the tier decision.' Add rows 'Speaking centre | TO NAME by 2026-10-31, with their private-candidate and NEA deadlines' and 'Weekly Spanish minutes | TO SET'. Under Checkpoint duties: Dec 2026 Listening + Reading Foundation sample papers (June 2026 series, the only real one), reported as component percentages with no grade; Mar 2027 full Foundation mock including a live-judged speaking mock recorded as such. Set the subject row's tier to match, or add 'intention' to its label so a reader knows it is not confirmed. The thresholds (30 topics, 31 Jan) are placeholders for the parent to set; the dates are the point.
findings.evidence_needed: Policy: JCQ private-candidate entry deadlines for summer 2027 and AQA rules on centres conducting NEA speaking for external candidates (confirm with the centre); no research evidence needed

findings.title: The speed ramp is the fun and should stay, but above about 7x it measures reaction time and the tracker then records timeouts as words not known
findings.where: language-learning-platform/assets/app-template.jsx lines 507-523 (ramp), 552-575 (movement interval: an escaped word counts as a fail), 525-550 (three consecutive fails ends the game), 598-622 (history entry records score, fails, accuracy, topSpeed, date only), 692-807 (game-over screen shows counts, never the missed words)
findings.problem: The word crosses 111 ticks at speed x 10 ms per tick: 6.7 s per word at the start (shown as 4.0x), 2.2 s at 8.0x, 1.8 s at the 8.4x she has already reached. Every third correct answer drops 0.8 until 7.5x, then 0.1 per ten. A timeout and a wrong pick both go into `fails` and both arrive in the tracker as `incorrect`, so the 43 'not got' items cannot be split into 'did not know' and 'was too slow'. Three consecutive fails end the game, so at high speed games end on speed rather than knowledge. The game-over screen shows Correct / Missed / Best Score and the trend, but never which words were missed, so the moment she is most motivated to fix something she is shown nothing to fix. With three options the guess rate is one in three; chance-corrected, her 76.8% pooled accuracy is about 65% of items actually known.
findings.why_it_matters: Time pressure plus sudden death can drive impulsive guessing, which the recognition format rewards one time in three; that inflates the accuracy figure the tracker uses as evidence (see the promotion finding below). At the same time the ramp and the top-speed number are what she enjoys, so removing them would cost engagement. The fix is to instrument and soften, not remove.
findings.proposal: (a) Split the count: keep `fails` for the game but add `timeouts` and `wrong` to the history entry and to the reported metrics (metrics_schema for spanish_gallery becomes ['top_speed' => 'number', 'timeouts' => 'number']), and set each item's note to 'timeout' or 'wrong'. (b) On the game-over screen, list the missed words under the score with a 'Practise these (no timer)' button that runs a short untimed round on exactly those words and logs it as a second run; this turns the fail into the next step, the analogue of the maths skill's 'what's one thing you could write down?'. (c) Offer a speed choice on the start screen, 'Steady (caps at 6x)' and 'Turbo (the current ramp)', both always available so nothing is withheld, and record which was used in metrics. (d) Fix the stale closure so the ramp uses the post-increment score (the `score % 3` test at line 513 reads the pre-increment value).
findings.evidence_needed: Time pressure and impulsive responding in ADHD; gamification and immediate feedback effects on engagement and accuracy for ADHD learners; recognition vs recall testing effects

findings.title: Bug: once a second set exists, the last 20% of every set never appears in the gallery and the last 40% never in the chat
findings.where: language-learning-platform/assets/app-template.jsx lines 64-85 (getMixedVocabulary), used at line 466 (gallery, 0.8) and line 917 (chat, 0.6)
findings.problem: `const currentCount = Math.floor(current.length * currentPercent); const previousCount = current.length - currentCount; const mixed = [...current.slice(0, currentCount)];` takes the first N words of the current set deterministically, then pads with random earlier words. For a 10-word set the gallery pool is words 1-8 and previous words; words 9-10 are only ever seen in flashcards. For a 20-word set, words 17-20 are excluded from the gallery and 13-20 from the chat. The template comment ('80% current set + 20% previous sets') describes a proportion, not a truncation. She is on set 1 today so it has not bitten yet; it bites the moment set 2 is added, which is the next thing the skill will do.
findings.why_it_matters: Silent gaps in what gets drilled are the opposite of a plan: a word at the end of a set would be logged as never missed because it is never shown, and a spaced review queue built on item history would trust that.
findings.proposal: Replace lines 73-84 with: `const extra = Math.ceil(current.length * (1 - currentPercent)); const mixed = [...current]; for (let i = 0; i < extra; i++) { mixed.push(previous[Math.floor(Math.random() * previous.length)]); } return mixed;` so every current word is always in the pool and earlier words are added on top in the intended proportion. Add a line to SKILL.md step 7 (Validate): 'check every word of the current set can appear in the gallery'.

findings.title: Flashcards have no self-rating, so spanish_flashcards can never produce a meaningful run and there is no production-side check
findings.where: language-learning-platform/assets/app-template.jsx lines 271-420 (completedCards is set on first flip; 'Progress: {completedCount} / {flashcards.length}'; welcome copy line 222 'Track your progress'); php/lib/practice.php line 33 (spanish_flashcards, metrics_schema [])
findings.problem: A card counts as 'completed' when it has been flipped once, whatever she knew. There is no 'got it / not yet', no shuffle (cards are in set order every time), and no way to recycle a missed card. A flashcards run logged to the tracker can therefore only ever be attempted = correct, which is why session 5 could only say '10 flashcards reviewed'. Every game mode is recognition; nothing asks her to produce the Spanish.
findings.why_it_matters: The gallery is recognition with a one-in-three guess rate; the promotion rules need a production check at about 70-80% to justify 'developing' and 'secure'. Self-rated recall is the cheapest honest production check and it is exactly the input a Leitner-style review needs (finding BUILD 2).
findings.proposal: On the back of each card add 'Got it' and 'Not yet' (keyboard right/left), default cards face English-first with the Spanish to recall (a toggle keeps the current direction), shuffle on start, recycle 'Not yet' cards to the end of the deck until each has been got once, and end the run with a summary that logs attempted / correct (first time) / correct_after_retry (got on a later pass) / incorrect (never), with items carrying prompt, outcome and note 'flash-not-yet'. Rename 'Reset All' to 'Shuffle and restart'.
findings.evidence_needed: Retrieval practice vs re-reading (testing effect); metacognitive self-rating accuracy in adolescents, and any ADHD-specific data on judgement-of-learning calibration

findings.title: The 4 Sep record disagrees with itself, and two topics were promoted on a recognition game whose misses point the other way
findings.where: live tracker: session 5 (2026-09-04) '40/50 correct overall (80%)... top speed 8.2x' vs practice run 4 (2026-09-04) '17 attempted, 13 first time, 4 not got, 76.5%'; T04 and G22 'Not started → Developing (session 5)'; gcse-progress-tracker/SKILL.md status rules lines 70-71 ('gap/notstarted → developing: topic taught + practice at roughly the developing bar with support'); README 'never moves a topic status — status moves through sessions only'
findings.problem: The same afternoon is recorded twice with different numbers: 40/50 in the session summary and topic evidence, 13/17 in the only practice run logged that day (and 8.2x vs a best of 8.4x on 18 Aug). Either games were played that were never logged as runs, or the summary is wrong; nothing cross-checks the two. On that evidence G22 'Present stem-change clusters' was promoted to developing, yet the misses listed in the same line (juega al, juegas al, juego al...) are precisely the jugar person-ending point: the evidence contradicts the promotion. No teaching is recorded for either topic. 'Practice never moves a status' holds in the service, but a session that wraps the practice moves it with the same numbers.
findings.why_it_matters: The tracker is the source of truth the skills are told to trust over memory. If it can hold two figures for one afternoon and a 'developing' that a re-test would immediately demote, the plan built on it inherits the error, and a demotion later reads to her as going backwards.
findings.proposal: For the parent: reconcile session 5 with tracker_amend_session or log the missing runs (not done in this review). For the skills: add to spanish.md under Promotion thresholds: 'A Shooting Gallery score is three-option recognition with a one-in-three guess rate. It never promotes a G-strand topic on its own and promotes a T-strand topic only alongside a production check (self-rated flashcards or typed recall) at 70% or better. Quote both in the evidence.' For the service: when tracker_log_session cites app practice, have the progress-tracker skill call tracker_list_practice(since: session date) and refuse to write a summary figure that has no matching run. Hosting the app on the tracker domain so it POSTs runs itself (BUILD 2) removes the transcription step that creates the mismatch.
findings.evidence_needed: None for the reconciliation; for the rule, recognition vs recall as evidence of learning (testing-effect literature)

findings.title: The 'spec conquered' badge is scored over all 100 topics including 27 Higher-only ones, so a complete Foundation preparation reads 49%
findings.where: php/lib/dashboard.php line 164 `$pct = $topics ? (int) round(($pts / (count($topics) * 3)) * 100) : 0;` with STATUS_POINTS in php/lib/store.php lines 30-35 (developing 1, secure 2, examready 3); live header '1% of the specification covered'
findings.problem: Two developing topics score 2 of 300 points, shown as 1%. On a Foundation pathway the 27 H-only topics (G41-G65, S16, P07) contribute nothing, so every F-pathway topic secure gives 146/300 = 49% and every one examready gives 73%. The single number she sees can never approach 100 on the tier she is most likely to sit, and it moves by 0.33 points per topic step, which at the seed's granularity means weeks between visible changes. The T-strand themes (each hundreds of words) will sit at 'developing' for months however much vocabulary she learns inside them.
findings.why_it_matters: The README's own rationale is that the chart exists 'because she likes seeing progress'. A progress figure that is structurally stuck near zero and capped below 100 does the opposite for a learner who runs on visible progress. This is a signal problem, not a data problem.
findings.proposal: Denominate the badge on the subject's intended tier: count only topics whose tier includes the subject row's tier (tier = 'F' counts F and F/H topics), and show the Higher-only remainder as a second small figure ('Higher extras: 0 of 27'). Add per-theme vocabulary movement from practice items once BUILD 2 lands: a 'words secure' count per T ref (words with box >= 2) shown on the topic chip, so T04 can read 'developing · 14 words secure' and change every session. Keep the golden snapshot rule: this is a dashboard change, not a scoreboard change.
findings.evidence_needed: Goal-gradient and progress-feedback effects on persistence; ADHD and reward-delay sensitivity (visible short-horizon progress)

findings.title: The marker's student file is the right idea but not yet sized or worded for a 13-year-old with ADHD who has not been taught most of the grammar
findings.problem: Current text: 'Include the summary, a per-question marks grid, a "where you lost marks" table giving **the grammar point and a hint only**, and a prioritised revision list.' and 'the student file names the structure ("preterite endings on -er verbs"), never the answer'. There is no cap on the length of the revision list, no requirement to say what went well, no plain-language rule, no link from a gap to the tracker topic or the app set that drills it, and no tone rule (the maths tutor skill has 'no walls of text'). With 98 topics notstarted, a hint on an untaught point ('preterite endings on -er verbs') is not something she can re-work; it reads as something she should have known.
findings.why_it_matters: Feedback works when it is specific, short and actionable; a full list of every grammar point lost, in examiner language, to a 13-year-old with ADHD is a list she will not read. The marker is also the only place the pipeline converts a paper into next steps, so its student file is effectively her plan for the following fortnight.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the student-file bullet as: 'Include the summary; the per-question marks grid; one line first on what worked (a descriptor met, a time frame used, a translation element carried); a "where you lost marks" table capped at THREE rows, each giving the pattern in plain words with a fresh example of the pattern that is not from the paper ("past-tense endings for -er verbs: comer → comí, comiste, comió"), the tracker ref (G29) and the app set that drills it; and a revision list of at most three items. Where the point has not been taught yet (status notstarted in tracker_get_state), say so: "we have not done this yet — it goes on the plan", never a hint that implies she should have known it. Tone: warm, brief, no walls of text; mistakes are information.' Keep the full gap list in the teacher file, where it belongs.
findings.evidence_needed: Feedback effectiveness (specific, task-focused, limited volume; Hattie & Timperley 2007, Wisniewski et al. 2020); working-memory load and list length for ADHD learners

findings.title: The AI Chat is pitched at 'a 12-year-old Key Stage 3 student', scores API failures as correct, and has no AQA task shapes
findings.where: language-learning-platform/assets/app-template.jsx lines 264 ('Key Stage 3 {LANGUAGE_NAME} • Vocabulary Practice'), 932 and 975 ('You are helping a 12-year-old Key Stage 3 student practice ${LANGUAGE_NAME} vocabulary'), 921-927 (promptTypes), 987-994 (binary JSON verdict), 1088-1095 (catch branch: 'Great try! Keep practicing! 🎉', correct: true, score incremented)
findings.problem: She is 13 and on the GCSE spec, so the model is told to pitch a year younger and to a different key stage. The verdict is a single correct/incorrect, so a sentence with a good time frame and one agreement slip is 'Not quite' in red. When the API call fails the code records a correct answer, so a spanish_chat run logged from this screen can be inflated by outages. None of the five prompt types is a role-play (five tasks x 2 marks), a photo card, or the four compulsory questions, which are the speaking tasks she will actually face, and the spanish_chat source has an empty metrics schema so it cannot carry the appendix's own behavioural metric (time frames).
findings.why_it_matters: The chat is the only production mode and the only place a scaffolded speaking-shaped task could live. Binary red/green feedback on every attempt is discouraging where partial credit is the exam's own rule ('message partially conveyed = 1').
findings.proposal: Add `const STUDENT = { age: 13, level: 'GCSE (AQA 8692)' }` and use it in both prompts and the footer. Replace promptTypes with role_play (five bullet tasks, 2 marks each), photo_card (describe, then two questions), four_questions, and conversation. Change the evaluation JSON to `{ conveyed: 0|1|2, time_frames: ["present","past","future"], major_errors: n, minor_errors: n, feedback, suggestion }`, show conveyed as 'Message got across / partly / not yet' rather than a red cross, and log runs with metrics { time_frames: n, tasks_conveyed: n } after adding those keys to spanish_chat's metrics_schema. In the catch branch do not touch the score and say the check failed.
findings.evidence_needed: Corrective feedback in L2 (partial-credit, explicit vs implicit; Lyster & Saito 2010); AQA role-play and photo-card marking (policy, already in the assessment reference)

findings.title: The build skill never mentions tracker_log_practice, so the app-to-tracker link depends on a free-text summary the template does not produce
findings.where: language-learning-platform/SKILL.md lines 150-159 (step 8) and 26-49 (template description); app-template.jsx lines 598-622 (history entry: score, fails, accuracy, topSpeed, date); README 'Ingest is one batched call at the end of a session... the model makes the call'
findings.problem: Step 8 says 'Consider logging the coverage (e.g. via `tracker_update_topic` / `tracker_log_session`, following the `maths-progress-tracker` / `gcse-tracker-dashboard` skill conventions)'. The skill named does not exist (it is gcse-progress-tracker), practice logging is not mentioned anywhere in any skill (a grep for log_practice, client_run_id and the three source keys across every SKILL.md returns nothing), and the template keeps no record of missed words, so there is nothing for the model to transcribe except what she remembers. The README's design ('the Spanish app supplies items only for the words missed') is therefore not implemented by the template the skill tells people to copy.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the seam that produced the 40/50 vs 13/17 mismatch and the garbled prompt. Every build above depends on runs and items arriving complete and consistent.
findings.proposal: Add a step 9 'Report practice' to SKILL.md with the exact call shape: one run per game, `client_run_id` = `${setNumber}-${startedAt ISO}`, source spanish_gallery / spanish_flashcards / spanish_chat, label = the set name, attempted/correct/incorrect from the game, duration_seconds, metrics { top_speed, timeouts }, items for every word { prompt, outcome, note, topic_ref }. Add to the template's game-over screen a 'Copy session report' button that emits that JSON (and keep it in window.storage under a pending-reports key until it has been logged), so the model pastes a structured block rather than reconstructing a summary. Fix the stale name to gcse-progress-tracker. Add to the template's history entry the arrays `missed` and `timeouts` so the record exists even when nothing is copied.

findings.title: The marker's logging example uses a topic ref that means something else in the live syllabus
findings.where: gcse-spanish-marker/SKILL.md Step 9 lines 184-201, and its own warning at lines 64-67
findings.problem: The example logs `{ number: "4", score: 7, max: 10, topic_ref: "G12", question: "Translation into Spanish, 5 sentences", ... note: "Grid1 11/15 ticks = 4; Grid2 3 — preterite endings wrong in 2 of 5 sentences" }`. In the live subject G12 is 'Subject pronouns and omission'; translation into Spanish is S14 and the preterite is G29. Step 1 warns that refs must come from tracker_get_state because an unrecognised ref 'drops silently out of the per-topic breakdown'; the example teaches the opposite habit, and a marker that copies it would credit a translation loss to pronouns.
findings.why_it_matters: The per-topic marks-lost table is what drives the fortnight after a mock; one wrong ref in the worked example propagates into every paper marked from it.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the example question as `{ number: "4", score: 7, max: 10, topic_ref: "S14", question: "Translation into Spanish, 5 sentences", answer: "…as written…", note: "Grid1 11/15 ticks = 4; Grid2 3 — grammar loss G29: preterite regular endings wrong in 2 of 5 sentences" }` and add one sentence: 'Log the task ref (S-strand) as topic_ref and name the grammar ref in the note, or log the grammar ref where the question is a pure grammar item (F Q3).' Also fix the frontmatter's '15 tools' claim at line 224 (the service exposes 21).
